programs.nl_rule:
The input grid has a uniform background color with several blue (B) cells scattered at various positions. These blue cells serve as seed points for a cross-based transformation.

For each blue (B) cell in the input: (1) Extend a full cross from that cell — fill its entire row and entire column with blue (B). (2) Replace the original B cell itself with red (R). (3) Place green (G) on the four diagonal neighbors of the original B position (one step up-left, up-right, down-left, down-right), but only if that diagonal cell falls within grid bounds. When a cell would receive both a green (G) marking and lies on a blue cross line from another seed, blue takes priority — blue crosses override green. Red and green never conflict since green is placed on diagonals while red sits at cross intersections. All cells not affected by any of these rules remain the background color.

The grid dimensions are the same in input and output. The background is a single uniform color (whichever non-blue color fills the input). The coordinate system is row-column with (0,0) at top-left. Grids can be any rectangular size. Blue seed points can appear anywhere in the grid.
